correctness.rationale: Under T-periodic bounded rates and positive multiplicative pulses, q=c/f, κ=(bf−ce)/f>0, Γy>0, Γx=qΓy, define periodic Φ by (a−qd) and pulse ratios α/β^q. For R=x/y^q, exact inter-pulse derivative d log R/dt=(a−qd)−κx and matching pulse ratios make Z=R/Φ pulse-continuous, with Z^(-1)(t)=R(0)^(-1)+κ∫₀ᵗΦy^q. Boundedness plus the resident positive net growth Γy rule out a bounded integral (which would force both populations to zero yet positive per-period y growth). Thus x→0; scalar impulsive logistic upper/lower comparison gives y→y*, and periodic Cesaro gives t x(t)−P(t)/(κPbar)→0. The exact log ratio prevents a positive periodic coexistence orbit. Independently reproduced the analytic example resident y*(0)=0.35872707857399 and distinct amplitudes 1.16905257454892 vs 0.82654975868862 for same product pulse schedules. Numerics do not prove infinite-time limit.
